1	/**
2	 * Pure budget vocabulary: the enforced cap names, the durable breach and
3	 * pricing payloads with their `SessionEventMap` declarations, the deployment
4	 * pricing entry, and the spend record the log fold produces. Kept free of
5	 * cordis, agent, and service imports so the fold, the plugin, and the
6	 * invariant companion share one home.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
9	 */
10	
11	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	
14	/** One enforced cap name; also the `Config` key that sets it. */
15	export type BudgetCapId =
16	  | 'maxInputTokens'
17	  | 'maxOutputTokens'
18	  | 'maxTotalTokens'
19	  | 'maxWallMs'
20	  | 'maxCostEur'
21	
22	/** EUR per one million tokens for one `provider/model` route. */
23	export interface BudgetRoutePricing {
24	  /** EUR per one million billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes). */
25	  readonly inputEurPerMillionTokens: number
26	  /** EUR per one million output tokens. */
27	  readonly outputEurPerMillionTokens: number
28	}
29	
30	/**
31	 * Session spend folded from the durable log. Token counts and cost cover every
32	 * `assistant/message` that carried provider `usage`; `wallMs` spans the log's
33	 * first and last event times, so it counts idle gaps between events but not
34	 * time elapsed since the newest event.
35	 */
36	export interface BudgetSpend {
37	  /** Billed input tokens: uncached input plus cache reads and writes. */
38	  readonly inputTokens: number
39	  /** Output tokens, reasoning output included as the provider reported it. */
40	  readonly outputTokens: number
41	  /** {@link inputTokens} plus {@link outputTokens}. */
42	  readonly totalTokens: number
43	  /** Milliseconds between the log's first and last event times; `0` for an empty log. */
44	  readonly wallMs: number
45	  /** EUR priced from the configured table; usage on an unpriced route adds nothing. */
46	  readonly costEur: number
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Ceilings recorded on one session's own log. Every cap is optional; a cap the
51	 * record omits leaves the deployment's configured value in force.
52	 */
53	export interface BudgetCaps {
54	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in this session. */
55	  readonly maxInputTokens?: number
56	  /** Output tokens allowed in this session. */
57	  readonly maxOutputTokens?: number
58	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in this session. */
59	  readonly maxTotalTokens?: number
60	  /** Milliseconds this session's log may span between its first and last event. */
61	  readonly maxWallMs?: number
62	  /** EUR this session's priced routes may cost; an unpriced route contributes nothing to it. */
63	  readonly maxCostEur?: number
64	}
65	
66	/** The durable record of one cap that stopped the next model request. */
67	export interface BudgetBreach {
68	  /** The cap that tripped. */
69	  readonly cap: BudgetCapId
70	  /** Spend measured from the log at the moment the step was stopped. */
71	  readonly measured: number
72	  /** The configured value {@link measured} exceeded. */
73	  readonly limit: number
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * One `assistant/message` event whose provider accounting is present. The
78	 * pricing helpers select and return this narrowed form, so a caller holding one
79	 * reads `usage` without repeating the presence check.
80	 */
81	export type AccountedMessage = SessionEvent<'assistant/message'> & { data: { usage: TokenUsage } }
82	
83	/** The durable price of one step, in the rates the configured table held. */
84	export interface UsagePriced {
85	  /** The turn that owned the priced step. */
86	  readonly turn: number
87	  /** The priced step within {@link turn}. */
88	  readonly step: number
89	  /** Provider of the route that served the step. */
90	  readonly provider: string
91	  /** Model of the route that served the step. */
92	  readonly model: string
93	  /** Billed input tokens: uncached input plus cache reads and writes. */
94	  readonly inputTokens: number
95	  /** Output tokens as the provider reported them. */
96	  readonly outputTokens: number
97	  /** EUR per one million billed input tokens applied to this step. */
98	  readonly inputEurPerMillionTokens: number
99	  /** EUR per one million output tokens applied to this step. */
100	  readonly outputEurPerMillionTokens: number
101	  /** EUR this step cost at the recorded rates. */
102	  readonly costEur: number
103	  /** Digest of the whole pricing table these rates came from. */
104	  readonly pricingDigest: string
105	}
106	
107	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
108	  interface SessionEventMap {
109	    /**
110	     * Ceilings this one session runs under, recorded by whoever created it for
111	     * a narrower purpose than the deployment's own configuration. The caps the
112	     * policy enforces are the configured caps tightened by the latest record in
113	     * the log: a cap only this record carries applies as written, and a cap
114	     * both carry applies at the smaller of the two, so a record can never buy a
115	     * session more budget than its deployment configured.
116	     */
117	    'budget/caps': BudgetCaps
118	    /**
119	     * One configured session budget stopped the step that was about to make a
120	     * model request: the cap that tripped, the spend measured from the events
121	     * preceding this one, and the configured value that spend exceeded. The
122	     * step is rejected after this event, so the record is the only durable
123	     * explanation for a turn that ends without a model call.
124	     */
125	    'budget/breach': BudgetBreach
126	    /**
127	     * One `assistant/message` of a priced route — a `provider/model` the
128	     * configured pricing table names — priced at the rates that table held:
129	     * `costEur = (inputTokens * inputEurPerMillionTokens + outputTokens *
130	     * outputEurPerMillionTokens) / 1_000_000`, with `pricingDigest` naming the
131	     * table version those rates came from. A route the table does not name gets
132	     * no event, so cost per session replays from the log for exactly the steps
133	     * the deployment had priced when they ran.
134	     */
135	    'usage/priced': UsagePriced
136	  }
137	}

1	/**
2	 * Environment runner: the automated validator that runs one registered
3	 * environment as one fresh session. It stamps the session with the
4	 * environment it runs, authors the completion standard from the environment's
5	 * checks, has each attempt implemented either by the session's own model route
6	 * or by an out-of-band coding agent started through the subagent seam, restores
7	 * the fixture's immutable paths and executes the checks through the shell
8	 * executor after each attempt, records the run, and completes the goal only
9	 * under a certificate. The
10	 * [environment-runner](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md)
11	 * and [external-implementer](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md)
12	 * Agent Notes own the design rationale.
13	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner
14	 */
15	
16	import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
17	import { cp, mkdir, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
18	import { dirname, isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'
19	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
20	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
21	import { installModelSelection } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
22	import type { Agent, AgentSampling } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
23	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
24	import { ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION, environmentContentHashes, isSeed, ROUTE_IMPLEMENTER } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
25	import type {
26	  EnvironmentDefinition,
27	  EnvironmentId,
28	  EnvironmentRunModel,
29	  EnvironmentRunStamp,
30	  EnvironmentTask,
31	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
32	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
33	import type { GoalId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
34	import { assertNever, createUserMessage, HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
35	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
36	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
37	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
38	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
39	import type { ShellExecSpec, ShellRunResult } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-shell'
40	import { runsOutOfProcess } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
41	import type { SubagentRuntime } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
42	import { caseChannelDigest, CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS, hashWorkspaceTree } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
43	import type {
44	  CaseExitClass,
45	  CertificateIsolation,
46	  CheckCase,
47	  CheckCaseChannel,
48	  CheckCaseComparator,
49	  CheckCaseExpectation,
50	  CheckCaseInput,
51	  CheckCaseNormalizer,
52	  CheckResult,
53	  DirectiveCluster,
54	  DirectiveRequest,
55	  FailedCheckCase,
56	  StandardCheck,
57	  StandardRef,
58	  StandardView,
59	  VerificationCertificate,
60	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
61	import type {
62	  EnvironmentRunAttempt,
63	  EnvironmentRunImplementer,
64	  EnvironmentRunReport,
65	  EnvironmentRunRequest,
66	} from './types.ts'
67	
68	export type * from './types.ts'
69	
70	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
71	  interface Context {
72	    environmentRuns: EnvironmentRunner
73	  }
74	}
75	
76	/** Stable error codes of a refused or broken run. */
77	export type EnvironmentRunErrorCode =
78	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT'
79	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_SEED'
80	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE'
81	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE'
82	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT'
83	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED'
84	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST'
85	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_REFERENCE'
86	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_RESERVATION'
87	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE'
88	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNCONFINED'
89	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED'
90	
91	/** Error returned by the environment runner boundary. */
92	export class EnvironmentRunError extends HarnessError {
93	  /**
94	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
95	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
96	   */
97	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
98	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
99	  constructor(message: string, code: EnvironmentRunErrorCode) {
100	    super(message, code)
101	  }
102	}
103	
104	/** Deployment choices of the runner, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
105	export interface Config {
106	  /** Isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs; written into every certificate and stamp. */
107	  isolation: CertificateIsolation
108	  /** Implementer turns before the run is reported uncertified; each is followed by one validation. */
109	  maxAttempts?: number
110	  /** Round cap handed to goal creation; absent applies the goal service default. */
111	  maxGoalRounds?: number
112	  /** Timeout override for each check command and each case, capped by the executor; absent applies the executor default. */
113	  checkTimeoutMs?: number
114	  /** Bound of each evidence string and of the directive detail. */
115	  evidenceMaxChars?: number
116	  /** Maximum failed cases one check result lists; the rest are counted and not named. */
117	  maxFailedCases?: number
118	  /**
119	   * Nucleus-sampling mass between 0 and 1 every request of every run asks for.
120	   * It is a deployment choice rather than a per-run one: a suite compares runs
121	   * only while every cell samples the same way. Absent leaves the
122	   * composition's own sampling in place.
123	   */
124	  topP?: number
125	}
126	
127	/** The runner's choices with every default applied. */
128	export interface ResolvedConfig {
129	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
130	  readonly maxAttempts: number
131	  readonly maxGoalRounds: number | undefined
132	  readonly checkTimeoutMs: number | undefined
133	  readonly evidenceMaxChars: number
134	  readonly maxFailedCases: number
135	  readonly topP: number | undefined
136	}
137	
138	/**
139	 * Apply the runner's defaults to a validated config.
140	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
141	 * @returns the resolved choices: one attempt, 2000 evidence characters, and 20 listed failed cases unless configured.
142	 */
143	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
144	  return {
145	    isolation: config.isolation,
146	    maxAttempts: config.maxAttempts ?? 1,
147	    maxGoalRounds: config.maxGoalRounds,
148	    checkTimeoutMs: config.checkTimeoutMs,
149	    evidenceMaxChars: config.evidenceMaxChars ?? 2000,
150	    maxFailedCases: config.maxFailedCases ?? 20,
151	    topP: config.topP,
152	  }
153	}
154	
155	/**
156	 * Apply the request's implementer default.
157	 * @param request - the run request as its caller wrote it.
158	 * @returns the implementer of every attempt: the session's own model route unless the request named a subagent provider.
159	 */
160	export function resolveImplementer(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): EnvironmentRunImplementer {
161	  return request.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
162	}
163	
164	/**
165	 * The name one implementer is stamped and folded under.
166	 * @param implementer - the resolved implementer.
167	 * @returns {@link ROUTE_IMPLEMENTER} for the session's own route, else the provider name.
168	 */
169	export function implementerName(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer): string {
170	  switch (implementer.kind) {
171	    case 'route':
172	      return ROUTE_IMPLEMENTER
173	    case 'subagent':
174	      return implementer.provider
175	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- EnvironmentRunImplementer is closed and every member is handled above */
176	    default:
177	      return assertNever(implementer, 'run implementer')
178	  }
179	}
180	
181	/** One run's implementer with the service a delegated one starts its children on already resolved. */
182	type RunImplementer =
183	  | { readonly kind: 'route' }
184	  | {
185	    readonly kind: 'subagent'
186	    readonly provider: string
187	    readonly label?: string
188	    /** The stamped model every child run must be started on, so the arm's model is the one that works. */
189	    readonly model: string
190	    readonly subagents: SubagentRuntime
191	  }
192	
193	/**
194	 * Characters a reserved check script's path may contain. The script is sourced
195	 * as the second word of the check command line, so the path must need no shell
196	 * quoting: quoting is dialect-specific and the runner does not know the composed
197	 * shell's dialect.
198	 */
199	const UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./\\-]+$/
200	
201	/** Key the check-owned digest records the reservation's tree under. */
202	const RESERVATION_KEY = '<reservation>'
203	
204	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one directory per check. */
205	const CHECKS_DIR = 'checks'
206	/** File inside a check's reserved directory holding its run instruction. */
207	const RUN_FILE = 'run'
208	/** File inside a check's reserved directory holding one case body per line. */
209	const CASES_FILE = 'cases.jsonl'
210	/** Reservation file holding the standard the current attempt measures. */
211	const STANDARD_FILE = 'standard.json'
212	/** Reservation subdirectory holding a held-out environment's fixture. */
213	const FIXTURE_DIR = 'fixture'
214	
215	/**
216	 * Reservation subdirectory holding the reference program of an environment
217	 * that declares `task.reference`. It sits inside the reservation, so the
218	 * check-owned digest already covers it and an implementer is denied it by the
219	 * same rule that denies the check scripts beside it.
220	 */
221	export const REFERENCE_DIR = 'reference'
222	
223	/**
224	 * File inside {@link REFERENCE_DIR} the validator's instrument sources to run
225	 * the reference, mirroring the `run` file of a reserved check. A fixed name
226	 * rather than a configured one: it is the convention an environment author and
227	 * the instrument agree on, not a deployment choice.
228	 */
229	export const REFERENCE_ENTRY = 'run'
230	
231	/** A check id usable as one path segment of its reserved directory. */
232	const SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/
233	
234	/**
235	 * Absolute path of one check's reserved directory, which holds its run script
236	 * and its case bodies. A check id that is not a single path segment, and a
237	 * script path the check command line cannot carry unquoted, are both refused.
238	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
239	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the directory's name.
240	 * @returns the absolute check directory.
241	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the id or the resulting path is unusable.
242	 */
243	function checkDirectory(runDirectory: string, checkId: string): string {
244	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {
245	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`check "${checkId}" cannot name a reserved script file`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
246	  }
247	  const directory = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)
248	  if (!UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD.test(join(directory, RUN_FILE))) {

267	/**
268	 * SHA-256 over one check-owned path: its tree when a directory, its bytes when
269	 * a file, and {@link ABSENT_DIGEST} when it is gone. Deleting a declared path
270	 * is as much a change to the check-owned set as rewriting it.
271	 * @param path - absolute path to digest.
272	 * @returns the digest, or the absent marker.
273	 */
274	async function hashCheckOwnedPath(path: string): Promise<string> {
275	  if (await isDirectory(path)) return hashWorkspaceTree(path)
276	  try {
277	    return createHash('sha256').update(await readFile(path)).digest('hex')
278	  } catch {
279	    // readFile rejects for a missing or unreadable path; either way the run

285	/**

287	 * when a barrier minted one, and every path the environment declared immutable,
288	 * each keyed by the name it is declared under.
289	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory, which immutable paths are relative to.
290	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
291	 * @param immutable - the environment's declared immutable paths.
292	 * @returns one digest over the whole set.
293	 */
294	async function hashCheckOwned(
295	  workspace: string,
296	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
297	  immutable: readonly string[],
298	): Promise<string> {
299	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
300	  if (runDirectory !== undefined) {
301	    hash.update(RESERVATION_KEY).update('\0').update(await hashWorkspaceTree(runDirectory)).update('\0')

303	  for (const path of immutable) {
304	    hash.update(path).update('\0').update(await hashCheckOwnedPath(join(workspace, path))).update('\0')

306	  return hash.digest('hex')

434	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
435	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
436	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted

439	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
440	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
441	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
442	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
443	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
444	  const marker = '\n…'
445	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
446	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
447	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
448	}

450	/** How one command ended, as the evidence states it. */
451	function exitLine(result: ShellRunResult): string {
452	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
453	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
454	  return `${exit}${cause}`
455	}

459	  const lines: string[] = []
460	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
461	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
462	  return lines
463	}

466	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
467	  return bound([exitLine(result), ...outputLines(result)].join('\n'), maxChars)

513	/**
514	 * Whether one captured stream disagrees with its expected digest. A truncated
515	 * stream disagrees whatever it holds: the executor dropped bytes the digest
516	 * covers, so the comparison cannot be made.
517	 */
518	function streamMismatch(
519	  stream: ShellRunResult['stdout'],
520	  expected: string | undefined,
521	  normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[],
522	): boolean {
523	  return stream.truncated || caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) !== expected

526	/**
527	 * The configured channels of one case whose observed value disagrees with the
528	 * case's expected digest, in the canonical channel order the log records.
529	 * @param body - the case that ran.
530	 * @param result - what the candidate produced.
531	 * @param scope - the absolute `treeScope` directory, absent for a check that declares none.
532	 * @returns the mismatching channels; empty when the case passed.
533	 */
534	async function caseMismatches(
535	  body: CheckCase,
536	  result: ShellRunResult,
537	  scope: string | undefined,
538	): Promise<CheckCaseChannel[]> {
539	  const { normalizers } = body.comparator
540	  const mismatched = new Set<CheckCaseChannel>()
541	  for (const channel of body.comparator.channels) {
542	    switch (channel) {
543	      case 'exit':
544	        if (result.exitCode !== body.expected.exitCode) mismatched.add(channel)
545	        break
546	      case 'stdout':
547	        if (streamMismatch(result.stdout, body.expected.stdoutSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
548	        break
549	      case 'stderr':
550	        if (streamMismatch(result.stderr, body.expected.stderrSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
551	        break
552	      case 'tree':
553	        // Authoring requires a treeScope for every check whose cases compare the tree.
554	        if (await hashWorkspaceTree(scope as string, normalizers) !== body.expected.treeSha256) mismatched.add(channel)
555	        break
556	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
557	      default:
558	        return assertNever(channel)
559	    }
560	  }
561	  return CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS.filter(channel => mismatched.has(channel))
562	}

588	/**
589	 * Run one case and capture all four channels: empty the case's `treeScope`,
590	 * stage its files, append its `argv` to the command, and feed its `stdin`.
591	 * Both executors of a case go through here — the runner measuring a candidate
592	 * and the instrument recording a reference — so what a case means is one
593	 * procedure rather than two that can drift.
594	 * @param shell - the composed shell executor.
595	 * @param execution - the resolved command, workspace, input, and bounds.
596	 * @returns the command's result and the tree scope it left.
597	 */
598	export async function captureCase(shell: Context['shell'], execution: CaseExecution): Promise<CaseCapture> {
599	  const scope = execution.treeScope === undefined ? undefined : join(execution.workspace, execution.treeScope)
600	  if (scope !== undefined) {
601	    await rm(scope, { recursive: true, force: true })
602	    await mkdir(scope, { recursive: true })
603	  }
604	  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(execution.input.files ?? {})) {
605	    const staged = join(execution.workspace, path)
606	    await mkdir(dirname(staged), { recursive: true })
607	    await writeFile(staged, content)
608	  }
609	  const stdin = execution.input.stdin
610	  const result = await shell.run(shell.resolve({
611	    command: [execution.command, ...execution.input.argv].join(' '),
612	    workdir: execution.workspace,
613	    timeoutMs: execution.timeoutMs,
614	    signal: execution.signal,
615	    ...stdin === undefined ? {} : { stdin },
616	  }))

620	/**
621	 * The expected digests one capture establishes for a comparator's configured
622	 * channels, which is what {@link caseMismatches} later compares a candidate
623	 * against. A truncated compared stream yields no digest for that channel: the
624	 * executor dropped bytes the digest would cover, so nothing could ever match it.
625	 * @param capture - what the reference produced for the case.
626	 * @param comparator - the channels compared and the normalizers applied first.
627	 * @returns the expectation, holding one value per configured channel that could be digested.
628	 */
629	export async function caseExpectation(
630	  capture: CaseCapture,
631	  comparator: CheckCaseComparator,
632	): Promise<CheckCaseExpectation> {
633	  const { normalizers } = comparator
634	  const { result } = capture
635	  const digest = (stream: ShellRunResult['stdout']): Record<string, never> | { sha256: string } => (
636	    stream.truncated ? {} : { sha256: caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) }
637	  )
638	  let expectation: CheckCaseExpectation = {}
639	  for (const channel of comparator.channels) {
640	    switch (channel) {
641	      case 'exit':
642	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...result.exitCode === null ? {} : { exitCode: result.exitCode } }
643	        break
644	      case 'stdout': {
645	        const value = digest(result.stdout)
646	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stdoutSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
647	        break
648	      }
649	      case 'stderr': {
650	        const value = digest(result.stderr)
651	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stderrSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
652	        break
653	      }
654	      case 'tree':
655	        // Only a comparator naming `tree` reaches here, and such a case is
656	        // executed with the scope its check declares.
657	        expectation = { ...expectation, treeSha256: await hashWorkspaceTree(capture.scope as string, normalizers) }
658	        break
659	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
660	      default:
661	        return assertNever(channel)
662	    }
663	  }
664	  return expectation
665	}

667	/** One rendered cluster with the check facts its line names. */
668	interface RenderedCluster extends DirectiveCluster {

675	/** Group one cased check's failed cases by the channels that disagreed and how the candidate ended. */
676	function clustersOf(check: StandardCheck, result: CheckResult): RenderedCluster[] {
677	  const cases = result.cases
678	  /* v8 ignore next -- only a cased result reaches here, and a cased result carries its tally */
679	  if (cases === undefined) return []
680	  const clusters = new Map<string, RenderedCluster>()
681	  for (const failed of cases.failed) {
682	    const key = `${failed.exitClass}|${failed.channels.join(',')}`
683	    const existing = clusters.get(key)
684	    clusters.set(key, {
685	      checkId: result.checkId,
686	      channels: failed.channels,
687	      count: (existing?.count ?? 0) + 1,
688	      weight: (existing?.weight ?? 0) + failed.weight,
689	      outcome: check.outcome,
690	      total: cases.total,
691	      weightTotal: cases.weightTotal,
692	      exitClass: failed.exitClass,
693	    })
694	  }
695	  return [...clusters.values()]

698	/**
699	 * One directive per failed run. A cased check contributes one line per failure
700	 * cluster, naming its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the
701	 * channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — never a case body, an
702	 * expected digest, or a byte of captured output. A check without cases
703	 * contributes its recorded evidence line.
704	 * @param failures - the run's failing results, in check order.
705	 * @param checks - the standard's active checks, supplying each outcome text.
706	 * @param maxChars - bound of the rendered detail.
707	 * @returns the directive, carrying `clusters` when a cased check failed.
708	 */
709	function describeFailures(
710	  failures: readonly CheckResult[],
711	  checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
712	  maxChars: number,
713	): DirectiveRequest {
714	  const lines: string[] = []
715	  const clusters: DirectiveCluster[] = []
716	  for (const failure of failures) {
717	    const check = checks.find(candidate => candidate.id === failure.checkId)
718	    if (check === undefined || failure.cases === undefined) {
719	      lines.push(failure.evidence)
720	      continue
721	    }
722	    for (const cluster of clustersOf(check, failure)) {
723	      clusters.push({ checkId: cluster.checkId, channels: cluster.channels, count: cluster.count, weight: cluster.weight })
724	      lines.push(`${cluster.outcome}: ${cluster.count} of ${cluster.total} cases failed (weight ${cluster.weight} of ${cluster.weightTotal}); mismatching channels: ${cluster.channels.join(', ')}; ${EXIT_PHRASE[cluster.exitClass]}`)
725	    }
726	  }
727	  return {
728	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
729	    detail: bound(lines.map((line, index) => `${index + 1}. ${line}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
730	    ...clusters.length === 0 ? {} : { clusters },
731	  }
732	}

764	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {

766	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
767	  ))
768	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
769	  const total: TokenUsage = {
770	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
771	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
772	  }

775	      const value = step[key]
776	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
777	    })
778	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)

874	  /**
875	   * Resolve the subagent runtime a delegated run starts its children on, before
876	   * any agent exists. A provider the composition does not hold, one whose child
877	   * this process cannot fence under a claim above `none`, and one that cannot
878	   * be told which model to run all fail here rather than at the first attempt,
879	   * when a stamped session would already exist for a run that can never
880	   * certify — or, for the model, would exist claiming an arm the child never
881	   * ran.
882	   * @param implementer - the implementer the request resolved to.
883	   * @param model - the run's stamped route, whose model every child run is started on.
884	   * @returns the run implementer with its service resolved.
885	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the named provider is not composed,
886	   *   runs outside this process under an isolation above `none`, or does not
887	   *   support the subagent seam's `model` capability.
888	   */
889	  private requireImplementer(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer, model: EnvironmentRunModel): RunImplementer {
890	    if (implementer.kind === 'route') return implementer
891	    const { provider: name, label } = implementer
892	    const subagents = this.ctx.get('subagents')
893	    if (subagents === undefined) {
894	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`implementer provider "${name}" is unavailable: this composition has no subagent service`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE')
895	    }
896	    const provider = subagents.getProvider(name)
897	    if (provider === undefined) {
898	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`implementer provider "${name}" is unavailable: no subagent provider is registered under that name`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE')
899	    }
900	    const isolation = this.resolved.isolation
901	    if (runsOutOfProcess(provider.capabilities) && isolation !== 'none') {
902	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`implementer provider "${name}" runs outside this process, where the read-barrier census cannot confine it, so it cannot implement a run declaring "${isolation}" isolation`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNCONFINED')
903	    }
904	    if (!provider.capabilities.model) {
905	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`implementer provider "${name}" cannot be told which model to run, so a run stamped with model "${model.model}" would measure whichever model that provider defaults to`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED')
906	    }
907	    return { kind: 'subagent', provider: name, ...label === undefined ? {} : { label }, model: model.model, subagents }
908	  }

910	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
911	  private async drive(
912	    agent: Agent,
913	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
914	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
915	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
916	    implementer: RunImplementer,
917	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
918	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
919	    await agent.whenIdle()
920	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
921	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
922	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
923	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
924	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
925	    })
926	    goals.disarm(agent)
927	    const authored = completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
928	    // Authorship validated every case against the reference it carries and kept
929	    // the reference alone; the bodies stay here, for the reservation and the
930	    // per-case execution.
931	    const bodies = new Map(definition.checks.flatMap(check => (
932	      check.caseBodies === undefined ? [] : [[check.id, check.caseBodies] as const]
933	    )))
934	    const immutable = definition.task.immutable ?? []
935	    // Stock the reservation and digest the check-owned set before the
936	    // implementer's first turn: that digest is what every later attempt is
937	    // compared against.
938	    await materializeChecks(runDirectory, authored, bodies)
939	    let checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
940	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
941	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
942	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
943	    try {
944	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
945	        await this.implement(agent, implementer, prompt, attempt, request.signal)
946	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
947	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
948	        if (await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable) !== checkOwned) {
949	          attempts.push(await this.recordTamper(agent, implementer, standard, ref, request.workspace, attempt))
950	          break
951	        }
952	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task)
953	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard, bodies)
954	        // The validator just rewrote its own directory, so the set it now owns
955	        // is the baseline the next attempt must still find.
956	        checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
957	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts, bodies)
958	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
959	          executor: 'runner',
960	          treeHash,
961	        })
962	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
963	        if (outcome.certified) {
964	          certificate = outcome.certificate
965	          const current = goals.get(agent)
966	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
967	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
968	          }
969	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
970	          break
971	        }
972	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, standard.checks, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
973	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
974	        prompt = followupText(directive)
975	      }
976	    } finally {
977	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
978	    }
979	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
980	    return {
981	      environment: definition.id,
982	      sessionId: agent.id,
983	      stamp,
984	      attempts,
985	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
986	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
987	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
988	    }
989	  }

1026	   * recorded rather than judged: whatever the child reports, the checks decide
1027	   * what the tree it left is worth, so a refusal or a transport failure ends

1091	    agent: Agent,
1092	    implementer: RunImplementer,
1093	    standard: StandardView,
1094	    ref: StandardRef,
1095	    workspace: string,
1096	    attempt: number,

1098	    const results: CheckResult[] = standard.checks.map(check => ({
1099	      checkId: check.id,
1100	      status: 'fail',

1105	      executor: 'runner',

1179	   * Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the
1180	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
1181	   * instruction inline. A check that carries cases runs once per case and its
1182	   * verdict follows the cases; every other check's verdict is its exit code.
1183	   */
1184	  private async execute(
1185	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
1186	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
1187	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
1188	    bodies: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CheckCase[]>,
1189	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
1190	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
1191	    for (const check of checks) {
1192	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
1193	      const command = script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`
1194	      const cases = bodies.get(check.id)
1195	      if (cases === undefined) {
1196	        const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(this.checkSpec(command, request))
1197	        results.push({
1198	          checkId: check.id,
1199	          status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
1200	          evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
1201	        })
1202	        continue
1203	      }
1204	      const run = await this.executeCases(check, cases, command, request)
1205	      // One bounded list of named failures serves both the durable tally and
1206	      // the evidence, so a run of hundreds of cases names the same subset twice.
1207	      const named = run.failures.slice(0, this.resolved.maxFailedCases)
1208	      results.push({
1209	        checkId: check.id,
1210	        status: run.passed === run.total ? 'pass' : 'fail',
1211	        evidence: casedEvidenceOf(run, named, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
1212	        cases: {
1213	          passed: run.passed,
1214	          total: run.total,
1215	          weightPassed: run.weightPassed,
1216	          weightTotal: run.weightTotal,
1217	          failed: named.map(failure => ({
1218	            id: failure.id,
1219	            weight: failure.weight,
1220	            channels: failure.channels,
1221	            exitClass: failure.exitClass,
1222	          })),
1223	        },
1224	      })

1240	   * Run one cased check case by case through {@link captureCase}, then compare
1241	   * every configured channel against the case's digest.
1242	   */
1243	  private async executeCases(
1244	    check: StandardCheck,
1245	    cases: readonly CheckCase[],
1246	    command: string,
1247	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
1248	  ): Promise<CasedCheckRun> {
1249	    const failures: CaseFailure[] = []
1250	    let passedCases = 0
1251	    let weightPassed = 0
1252	    for (const body of cases) {
1253	      const { result, scope } = await captureCase(this.ctx.shell, {
1254	        workspace: request.workspace,
1255	        command,
1256	        input: body.input,

1259	        ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
1260	      })
1261	      const channels = await caseMismatches(body, result, scope)
1262	      if (channels.length === 0) {
1263	        passedCases += 1
1264	        weightPassed += body.weight
1265	        continue
1266	      }
1267	      failures.push({ id: body.id, weight: body.weight, channels, exitClass: exitClassOf(result), result })
1268	    }
1269	    return {
1270	      passed: passedCases,
1271	      total: cases.length,
1272	      weightPassed,
1273	      weightTotal: cases.reduce((sum, body) => sum + body.weight, 0),

11	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
12	import type { SubagentStopReason } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
13	import type { CheckResult, VerificationCertificate } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
14	
15	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
16	  interface SessionEventMap {
17	    /**
18	     * One attempt of a delegated cell, appended after the child run settled
19	     * and before the runner validates the tree it left: which provider ran it,
20	     * the run's parent-scoped id, how it ended, the structured result it
21	     * returned, the model usage this process can account for, and the model and
22	     * spend the child's own backend reported. Log-only — it never enters model
23	     * history, and it is the cell session's only record of an implementer whose
24	     * own transcript stays in its product.
25	     *
26	     * The model the cell ASKED for is on the `environment/run` stamp, which the
27	     * runner also passes to the provider, so a reader comparing the two sees
28	     * whether the child ran the arm's model and which concrete version an alias
29	     * resolved to.
30	     */
31	    'environment/delegation': EnvironmentDelegation
32	  }
33	}
34	
35	/**
36	 * Who implements the work of one run: the session's own model route, driven
37	 * turn by turn as the runner has always driven it, or one out-of-band coding
38	 * agent started per attempt through the subagent seam.
39	 */
40	export type EnvironmentRunImplementer =
41	  | { readonly kind: 'route' }
42	  | {
43	    readonly kind: 'subagent'
44	    /** Registered `ctx.subagents` provider each attempt's child run starts on. */
45	    readonly provider: string
46	    /** Short display label persisted with a session-backed child; absent leaves the provider's own naming. */
47	    readonly label?: string
48	  }
49	
50	/**
51	 * Durable record of one delegated attempt. It is what the cell session states
52	 * about an implementer that produced no model-visible history of its own.
53	 */
54	export interface EnvironmentDelegation {
55	  /** One-based attempt this child run implemented. */
56	  readonly attempt: number
57	  /** Subagent provider that ran the child. */
58	  readonly provider: string
59	  /** Parent-scoped id of the child run; the child's session id for an in-process provider. */
60	  readonly runId: SessionId
61	  /** How the child run ended, in the subagent seam's terminal vocabulary. */
62	  readonly stopReason: SubagentStopReason
63	  /** Structured result the child returned, absent when it returned none. */
64	  readonly structured?: unknown
65	  /**
66	   * Model usage of an in-process child's own session, summed over its
67	   * assistant messages. Absent for a child this process cannot account for,
68	   * which is every out-of-process provider: its tokens are spent in another
69	   * product and never reach a log here.
70	   */
71	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
72	  /**
73	   * The model the child's own backend stated it ran, as that backend names it —
74	   * an in-process child's route model, an external product's full model id.
75	   * Absent when the provider reports none or the run ended before it did.
76	   * Against the requested model on the `environment/run` stamp it is what
77	   * decides whether a delegated measurement is labelled with the model that
78	   * produced it.
79	   */
80	  readonly reportedModel?: string
81	  /**
82	   * Token accounting the child's own backend reported for the run. It is the
83	   * only spend record an out-of-process child leaves, whose tokens are spent in
84	   * another product; {@link usage} covers an in-process one instead, so at most
85	   * one of the two is stated. Absent when the provider reported none.
86	   */
87	  readonly reportedUsage?: TokenUsage
88	  /**
89	   * Cost in US dollars as the child's own backend priced the run. It is a
90	   * foreign product's accounting rather than a harness pricing table, so it is
91	   * comparable across attempts of the same implementer and never summed with a
92	   * `usage/priced` cost. Absent when the provider reported none.
93	   */
94	  readonly reportedCostUsd?: number
95	}
96	
97	/** One request to run a registered environment as one fresh session. */
98	export interface EnvironmentRunRequest {
99	  /** Registered environment to run. */
100	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
101	  /** Existing absolute directory the session is rooted at; the task fixture is overlaid onto it. */
102	  readonly workspace: string
103	  /** Model route for this run; absent uses the composition's default model selection. */
104	  readonly model?: EnvironmentRunModel
105	  /**
106	   * Who does the work of each attempt; absent runs the session's own model
107	   * route. A delegated run is validated identically: only the way the
108	   * workspace reaches its next state changes.
109	   */
110	  readonly implementer?: EnvironmentRunImplementer
111	  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; absent means `0`. */
112	  readonly repetition?: number
113	  /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */
114	  readonly group?: string
115	  /** District the run belongs to, written into the stamp so exports can withhold it; absent for a run outside every district. */
116	  readonly district?: string
117	  /**
118	   * Checkpoint or policy the implementer route serves, as the deployment names
119	   * it, written into the stamp verbatim; absent for a route the deployment did
120	   * not version.
121	   */
122	  readonly policyVersion?: string
123	  /**
124	   * Sampling seed every request of the run asks for, a safe non-negative
125	   * integer written into the stamp; absent leaves the composition's own
126	   * sampling in place.
127	   */
128	  readonly seed?: number
129	  /** Aborts the implementer's turns and the check commands when it fires. */
130	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
131	}
132	
133	/**
134	 * One attempt: the implementer's turn followed by one run of the current
135	 * standard. The attempt's verdict is durable rather than reported: it is the
136	 * `verdict` of the `verification/run` this attempt recorded.
137	 */
138	export interface EnvironmentRunAttempt {
139	  /** One-based attempt number. */
140	  readonly attempt: number
141	  /** One result per active check, in the standard's check order; a tampered attempt executed none of them. */
142	  readonly results: readonly CheckResult[]
143	  /**
144	   * SHA-256 digest of the workspace as the validation began, after the fixture
145	   * was restored over it; a tampered attempt digests the workspace it refused
146	   * to measure, without restoring anything.
147	   */
148	  readonly treeHash: string
149	}
150	
151	/** Outcome of one environment run, returned after the session is flushed. */
152	export interface EnvironmentRunReport {
153	  /** Environment that was run. */
154	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
155	  /** Session the run created; its log is the durable record. */
156	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
157	  /** The `environment/run` stamp the session log carries, exactly as appended. */
158	  readonly stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp
159	  /** Every attempt in order; the last one decided `certified`. */
160	  readonly attempts: readonly EnvironmentRunAttempt[]
161	  /** Whether a run of the standard passed completely and the goal completed. */
162	  readonly certified: boolean
163	  /** Certificate of the passing run, present exactly when `certified` is `true`. */
164	  readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate
165	  /** Model usage summed over every assistant message of the session, absent when the model produced none. */
166	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
167	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of one experiment: the plan a digest freezes, the two arms, the
3	 * paired per-environment comparison, and the verdict, free of host-side
4	 * imports.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments/types
7	 */
8	
9	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
10	import type { EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
11	import type { TrajectorySink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories/types'
12	
13	/** Role one arm plays in a comparison; both roles run the same cells. */
14	export type ExperimentArmRole = 'baseline' | 'candidate'
15	
16	/**
17	 * One arm as a plan names it: the model route its cells run and who implements
18	 * them. An arm that names no implementer runs its own route, so a plan that
19	 * omits the field and one that spells `{ kind: 'route' }` out are one
20	 * experiment and freeze to one digest.
21	 */
22	export interface ExperimentArmPlan extends EnvironmentRunModel {
23	  /**
24	   * Who does the work of every cell of this arm — the arm's own model route,
25	   * or an out-of-band coding agent behind a registered subagent provider. The
26	   * cells, the checks, and the certificate are the same either way, so an arm
27	   * that delegates is comparable with one that does not.
28	   */
29	  readonly implementer?: EnvironmentRunImplementer
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Statistical choices frozen into the plan digest. They decide what the
34	 * comparison measures and what counts as promotable, so two plans that differ
35	 * in any of them are two experiments.
36	 */
37	export interface ExperimentThresholds {
38	  /** Resamples drawn per bootstrap interval. */
39	  readonly bootstrapResamples: number
40	  /** Coverage of every reported interval, between `0` and `1`. */
41	  readonly confidenceLevel: number
42	  /** Certificate-rate delta the overall interval's lower bound must exceed to promote. */
43	  readonly minimumDelta: number
44	  /** Tokens one cell may spend; the projection the token budget is checked against. */
45	  readonly cellTokenCap: number
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * One comparison to run: two arms over the same environments at the same
50	 * repetition indexes. A caller that froze the plan earlier passes the digest
51	 * it recorded back on {@link ExperimentPlan.digest}.
52	 */
53	export interface ExperimentPlan {
54	  /** Environments both arms run, each registered and named once. */
55	  readonly environments: readonly EnvironmentId[]
56	  /** Positive number of repetitions per environment and arm; repetition indexes start at zero. */
57	  readonly repetitions: number
58	  /** The reference arm. */
59	  readonly baseline: ExperimentArmPlan
60	  /** The arm under test. */
61	  readonly candidate: ExperimentArmPlan
62	  /** Existing absolute directory under which every cell gets its own fresh workspace directory. */
63	  readonly workspaceRoot: string
64	  /**
65	   * Checkpoint or policy both arms' routes serve, written into every cell's
66	   * run stamp verbatim; absent for routes the deployment did not version.
67	   */
68	  readonly policyVersion?: string
69	  /**
70	   * Base sampling seed both arms share, a safe non-negative integer. Each cell
71	   * samples with `seed + repetition`, so the paired repetitions of the two arms
72	   * differ only in the route; absent leaves sampling to the composition.
73	   */
74	  readonly seed?: number
75	  /** Digest the caller froze earlier; a value the recomputed digest does not equal is refused. */
76	  readonly digest?: string
77	  /** Aborts the remaining cells when it fires; started cells abort through the runner. */
78	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
79	  /** Destination of the result line; absent writes nothing and leaves the sessions as the only record. */
80	  readonly sink?: TrajectorySink
81	}
82	
83	/** One arm as it ran: its model route, its implementer, and the stamp `group` its sessions carry. */
84	export interface ExperimentArm {
85	  /** Model route every cell of this arm ran. */
86	  readonly model: EnvironmentRunModel
87	  /** Implementer every cell of this arm ran under, with the plan's default applied, so a stored result tells the arms apart alone. */
88	  readonly implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer
89	  /** `experiment-<digest>-<role>`, written into the `environment/run` stamp of every session of this arm. */
90	  readonly group: string
91	}
92	
93	/** Both arms of one experiment. */
94	export interface ExperimentArms {
95	  readonly baseline: ExperimentArm
96	  readonly candidate: ExperimentArm
97	}
98	
99	/** Percentile bootstrap interval of a delta at the plan's confidence level. */
100	export interface ConfidenceInterval {
101	  readonly lower: number
102	  readonly upper: number
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * One environment's paired comparison. Every rate, mean, and delta covers the
107	 * paired repetitions alone, so a repetition an arm failed to report changes
108	 * `pairs` and `unpaired` rather than silently shifting a rate.
109	 */
110	export interface ExperimentCell {
111	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
112	  /** Repetition indexes both arms reported. */
113	  readonly pairs: number
114	  /** Repetition indexes that did not pair because an arm produced no report. */
115	  readonly unpaired: number
116	  /** Certified fraction of the baseline arm over the paired repetitions, `0` without pairs. */
117	  readonly baselineRate: number
118	  /** Certified fraction of the candidate arm over the paired repetitions, `0` without pairs. */
119	  readonly candidateRate: number
120	  /** `candidateRate - baselineRate`. */
121	  readonly delta: number
122	  /** Bootstrap interval of `delta`, absent without pairs. */
123	  readonly interval?: ConfidenceInterval
124	  /** Candidate mean attempts minus baseline mean attempts over the paired repetitions. */
125	  readonly attemptsDelta: number
126	  /** Candidate minus baseline input tokens summed over the paired repetitions. */
127	  readonly inputTokenDelta: number
128	  /** Candidate minus baseline output tokens summed over the paired repetitions. */
129	  readonly outputTokenDelta: number
130	}
131	
132	/** Model usage summed over every reported cell of both arms, paired or not. */
133	export interface ExperimentSpend {
134	  readonly inputTokens: number
135	  readonly outputTokens: number
136	}
137	
138	/** What the overall interval says about the candidate. */
139	export type ExperimentVerdict = 'promote' | 'reject' | 'inconclusive'
140	
141	/**
142	 * Outcome of one experiment. The sessions grouped by `arms` carry the durable
143	 * evidence; this record is the fold over them.
144	 */
145	export interface ExperimentResult {
146	  /** Content digest of the frozen plan; both arm groups carry it. */
147	  readonly digest: string
148	  /** The two arms and the stamp group each ran under. */
149	  readonly arms: ExperimentArms
150	  /** One entry per environment, in plan order. */
151	  readonly cells: readonly ExperimentCell[]
152	  /** Paired repetition indexes over every environment; the bootstrap's units. */
153	  readonly seedsPaired: number
154	  /** Certificate-rate delta over every paired repetition, `0` without pairs. */
155	  readonly delta: number
156	  /** Bootstrap interval of `delta`, absent without pairs; the verdict reads it. */
157	  readonly interval?: ConfidenceInterval
158	  /** Model usage of both arms together. */
159	  readonly spend: ExperimentSpend
160	  /** Thresholds the digest froze, restated so a stored result is readable alone. */
161	  readonly thresholds: ExperimentThresholds
162	  readonly verdict: ExperimentVerdict
163	}

1	/**
2	 * Freezing one experiment plan: the content digest computed before any cell
3	 * runs, and the stamp `group` each arm's sessions carry so a later fold can
4	 * find them in the logs.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments/plan
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
11	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { ExperimentArmPlan, ExperimentArmRole, ExperimentPlan, ExperimentThresholds } from './types.ts'
13	
14	/**
15	 * Group namespace this package owns. A `group` starting with it names an
16	 * experiment arm, so no other producer may mint one.
17	 */
18	export const EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX = 'experiment-'
19	
20	/** Self-declared version of the digested plan fields; a change to what they cover changes it. */
21	const EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION = 3
22	
23	/** Arm roles in the order the digest and the runs take them. */
24	export const EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES: readonly ExperimentArmRole[] = ['baseline', 'candidate']
25	
26	const GROUP_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(${EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.join('|')})$`)
27	
28	/**
29	 * The implementer one arm runs under.
30	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
31	 * @returns the named implementer, or the arm's own model route when it names none.
32	 */
33	export function armImplementer(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): EnvironmentRunImplementer {
34	  return arm.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * One implementer as the digest takes it: the discriminant, the subagent
39	 * provider, and its label, each in a fixed position, so the key order a caller
40	 * happened to write cannot change the digest.
41	 */
42	function digestedImplementer(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer): readonly (string | null)[] {
43	  switch (implementer.kind) {
44	    case 'route':
45	      return [implementer.kind, null, null]
46	    case 'subagent':
47	      return [implementer.kind, implementer.provider, implementer.label ?? null]
48	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- EnvironmentRunImplementer is closed and every member is handled above */
49	    default:
50	      return assertNever(implementer, 'arm implementer')
51	  }
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what an experiment measures: the
56	 * two arms in role order, each with its model route and its implementer, the
57	 * environment ids sorted so a caller's listing order cannot change the
58	 * identity, the repetition count, the policy version and base seed both arms
59	 * ran under, and the thresholds. The deployment's token budget is deliberately
60	 * absent: it bounds what a deployment pays for, not what the comparison
61	 * measures. The policy version and the seed are present because both arms'
62	 * sessions are found in the logs by the groups this digest mints, so two
63	 * comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group.
64	 * @param plan - the arms, environments, repetitions, policy version, and seed to freeze.
65	 * @param thresholds - the resolved statistical choices to freeze with them.
66	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
67	 */
68	export function planDigest(plan: ExperimentPlan, thresholds: ExperimentThresholds): string {
69	  const content = JSON.stringify({
70	    version: EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION,
71	    arms: EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.map(role => [
72	      role,
73	      plan[role].provider,
74	      plan[role].model,
75	      digestedImplementer(armImplementer(plan[role])),
76	    ]),
77	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
78	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
79	    policyVersion: plan.policyVersion ?? null,
80	    seed: plan.seed ?? null,
81	    thresholds: [
82	      thresholds.bootstrapResamples,
83	      thresholds.confidenceLevel,
84	      thresholds.minimumDelta,
85	      thresholds.cellTokenCap,
86	    ],
87	  })
88	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * Stamp `group` one arm's sessions carry.
93	 * @param digest - the frozen plan digest.
94	 * @param role - which arm the group names.
95	 * @returns `experiment-<digest>-<role>`.
96	 */

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Test driver: boot the external-implementer composition, run the
 * training-eligible environments once each with the `spawn` subagent provider
 * as the implementer, run the same environments again on their own model route,
 * and print both fleet reports, the delegation events each delegated cell
 * session recorded, the facts of the certified delegated cell, and the
 * scoreboard folded from every persisted log, for the e2e's assertions.
 */

import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
import type { EnvironmentDelegation } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
import type { FleetCellOutcome, FleetPlan } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types'
import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'

const configPath = process.argv[2]
if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('external-implementer driver requires a config path')

const ctx = await boot('external-implementer-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
try {
  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
  const fleet = ctx.get('fleet')
  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
  if (fleet === undefined || scorekeeper === undefined || persistence === undefined) {
    throw new Error('external-implementer driver requires the fleet, the scorekeeper, and session persistence')
  }
  const plan = (group: string, implementer?: FleetPlan['implementer']): FleetPlan => ({
    environments: { filter: { heldOut: false } },
    models: [],
    repetitions: 1,
    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
    group,
    ...implementer === undefined ? {} : { implementer },
  })
  const delegated = await fleet.run(plan('external-implementer-e2e', { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'spawn', label: 'external' }))
  const routed = await fleet.run(plan('route-implementer-e2e'))

  const sessionOf = (outcome: FleetCellOutcome): SessionId => {

  if (certified === undefined) throw new Error('external-implementer driver expects one certified delegated cell')

    routed: { leaderboard: routed.leaderboard },
    delegations,
    facts,
    scoreboard,

# The Proving Ground bench: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in three
# domains, registered from their task.json files, run on the operator's Claude
# Code subscription through the harness's own agent loop (the LLM route) or
# through the product's own loop (the external implementer), and compared in
# frozen paired experiments. No cadence: the drivers beside this file run one
# plan each.
#
# The route serves three product models under one provider. Every arm of an
# experiment names one of them, so a comparison between models and a comparison
# between implementers both read from the same catalog. The product envelope
# around each query is the one model-visible input the log does not hold.
- id: llm-claude-code
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    models:
      - id: opus
        name: Claude Code opus
        productModel: opus
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: sonnet
        name: Claude Code sonnet
        productModel: sonnet
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: haiku
        name: Claude Code haiku
        productModel: haiku
        contextWindow: 200000
    effort: medium
    queryTimeoutMs: 300000

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor, for the CLI the route
# spawns per query, and for the product the external implementer spawns.
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

# The filesystem tools resolve paths against the cell session's cwd, which the
# runner sets to the cell workspace; the policy loads first so writes and edits
# require an observed file.
- id: fs-local
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'

- id: fs-observation-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy'

- id: tool-fs
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

- id: goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
  config:
    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
  config:
    maxChecks: 32
    maxTextChars: 4096

- id: environments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

- id: register-environments
  name: './register-environments.ts'

# The default route of a cell agent; an experiment arm or a fleet plan names the
# model explicitly, so this only decides what an unnamed request runs.
- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    model: sonnet

- id: subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'

# The product's own loop as an implementer, for the arm that measures it
# against the harness loop: unattended edits and the test command allowed,
# nothing else. Its spend is outside every limit this harness enforces.
- id: subagent-claude-code
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code'
  config:
    permissionMode: acceptEdits
    allowedTools:
      - 'Bash(node:*)'

# `isolation: none` is the only claim the external arm can serve; both arms run
# under the same claim so the certificates compare.
- id: environment-runner
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
  config:
    isolation: none
    maxAttempts: 3
    evidenceMaxChars: 2048

- id: fleet
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
  config:
    maxConcurrent: 2
    workspaceRetention: keep

- id: experiments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'
  config:
    bootstrapResamples: 2000
    confidenceLevel: 0.95
    minimumDelta: 0.05
    cellTokenCap: 600000
    tokenBudget: 200000000

# Village rule: unattended cells carry a session budget. A cell that has not

- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxTotalTokens: 1500000
    maxWallMs: 1200000

# @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A durable spend ceiling for one session: configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps, tightened by whatever caps the session's own log records, are measured against that log before every proposed step, and the first cap the log exceeds records a `budget/breach` event, blocks the session's goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every step a priced route served also records a `usage/priced` event, so what a session cost is a durable fact rather than an in-memory total. Nothing is measured in memory — the caps read the same durable events a replay reads, so a recorded breach or price is reproducible by anyone holding the log. Decision record: [the budget-policy Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-budget-policy.md).

## Config

```yaml
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxInputTokens: 2000000      # billed input: uncached input + cache reads + cache writes
    maxOutputTokens: 400000      # output tokens, provider-reported
    maxTotalTokens: 2400000      # input + output
    maxWallMs: 3600000           # span between the log's first and last event
    maxCostEur: 25               # priced routes only; needs a non-empty pricing table
    pricing:
      deepseek/deepseek-chat:
        inputEurPerMillionTokens: 0.25
        outputEurPerMillionTokens: 1.0
```

Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step and never reads the log. A cap is exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value: `0` stops the session at the first recorded spend, and a session exactly on budget keeps running.

Validation happens at plugin load, before any session can depend on a cap the policy could not enforce. A cap or rate that is not a finite non-negative number throws, and `maxCostEur` without a non-empty `pricing` table throws — an unpriced route has no cost cap, so a cost ceiling over an empty table would silently enforce nothing.

`pricing` keys are `provider/model`, matching the provenance each assistant message carries. A route absent from the table contributes its tokens to the token caps but nothing to `costEur`, so token caps remain the enforcement of last resort for a route whose price the deployment has not stated.

## Plugin contract (namespace: `budget-policy`)

A function/namespace plugin (`name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply`), not a service. It injects `ctx.agents` and registers one prepended `agent/pre-step` listener and one `agent/turn-stopping` listener; `ctx.goals` is read optionally through `ctx.get('goals')`, so the policy enforces identically in a composition without the goal domain.

The pre-step listener is prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run. On a breach it does not call `next()`: the chain short-circuits and the loop closes the turn with reason `blocked`, having opened no step.

`foldBudgetSpend(events, pricing)`, `measuredFor(spend, cap)`, `unpricedUsage(events, pricing)`, `foldSessionCaps(events)`, `tightenedCaps(configured, session)`, `BUDGET_CAP_ORDER`, and `pricingTableDigest(pricing)` are exported so a supervisor can recompute any recorded measurement, price, or enforced cap from the log.

### Measuring spend from the log

`assistant/message` is the single usage source: it carries a step's final provider accounting, so the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. A message without `usage` contributes nothing. Billed input is the disjoint sum of `inputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, and `cacheWriteTokens`; output is `outputTokens` as the provider reported it. Each message prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid-session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it.

`maxWallMs` measures the span between the log's first and last event times. It therefore counts idle gaps between events, including the gap across a process restart, but not time elapsed since the newest event — which is what makes the measurement a function of the log rather than of the clock at read time.

### Per-session caps

A session created for a narrower purpose than the whole deployment records its own ceilings as a `budget/caps` event carrying any subset of the five cap fields. The caps enforced for that session are the configured caps tightened by the latest `budget/caps` in its log: a cap only the record carries applies as written, a cap both carry applies at the smaller of the two, and a cap neither carries stays uncapped. A record can therefore only ever narrow what the deployment configured, which is what lets an orchestrator hand one session a slice of the deployment's budget without being able to grant it more.

The caps are folded from the log like the spend they bound, so a resumed session enforces exactly the caps its own log records and the model sees nothing: `budget/caps` reaches no model request. A `maxCostEur` recorded on a session whose routes the `pricing` table does not name measures against a cost of zero and therefore never trips, exactly as a configured cost cap does over an unpriced route.

### What a breach does

1. Appends `budget/breach` with the cap that tripped, the measured spend, and the configured value it exceeded. The caps are evaluated in the fixed order `maxInputTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `maxTotalTokens`, `maxWallMs`, `maxCostEur`, and the first one exceeded is the one recorded.
2. Blocks a current `active` goal through `ctx.goals.block` with code `budget-exhausted` and the message `Session budget <cap> exceeded: <measured> of <limit>.` The block is durable and disarms continuation, so a goal-round driver does not resume the goal afterwards. A composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current goal, or whose goal already left `active` still gets the breach record and the stopped turn.
3. Returns `{ kind: 'reject' }`, which ends the turn without opening a step.

Spend never decreases, so a later step in the same session breaches again: each stopped step records its own event, and the durable log states exactly how many attempts the exhausted budget turned away. Raising a cap and reloading the deployment is the way to resume.

### What a priced step records

`usage/priced` states the price of one `assistant/message` whose `provider/model` the `pricing` table names: the `turn` and `step` it prices, that route's `provider` and `model`, the `inputTokens` (billed input) and `outputTokens` it charges for, the `inputEurPerMillionTokens` and `outputEurPerMillionTokens` applied, the resulting `costEur = (inputTokens * inputEurPerMillionTokens + outputTokens * outputEurPerMillionTokens) / 1_000_000`, and a `pricingDigest`. The digest is the lowercase SHA-256 of the whole configured table — route keys ordered by code unit, each entry serialized as its input rate then its output rate — so a reader can tell which table version priced a step and one changed rate changes the digest. Rates travel in the record itself, which is what makes session cost replayable without the deployment configuration. A route the table does not name records nothing.

Which steps to price is read from the log, not remembered: a step is priced when its message carries `usage`, its route is priced, and no `usage/priced` in the log already carries its turn and step. A resumed session therefore prices exactly what its predecessor left unpriced, and never prices a step twice. The records are written at two points — inside the pre-step listener, before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is priced by the same step that records the breach; and at `agent/turn-stopping`, so the final step of a turn that closes normally is priced too.

A turn that ends by error or abort reaches neither point, so its last message stays unpriced until the session's next pre-step or stop boundary; a session abandoned in that state keeps one unpriced step in its log.

### Invariant companion

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy/invariant` recomputes each durable record independently. A breach's recorded `measured` must exceed `limit`, and for the log-derived caps it must equal this package's fold over exactly the events preceding the record; `maxCostEur` depends on the deployment pricing table, which the log does not carry, so a cost breach is checked only for the exceeded-its-limit relation. A price must cite an earlier `assistant/message` with the same turn and step whose billed tokens and route it reproduces exactly, its `costEur` must equal its own rates applied to its own tokens, and no earlier `usage/priced` may carry the same turn and step.

A `budget/caps` record may only tighten. The deployment's configured caps are not in the log, so the companion compares each cap against the caps the same session's earlier `budget/caps` records already fold to: raising one of those, or dropping it so the cap disappears, is rejected at append. Widening a cap the deployment configured is outside what the log can show and is refused by the enforcing fold instead, which never takes a recorded value above the configured one.

## Model Experience

### Stopped step

#### What the model sees

Nothing. A breach is decided before the step opens, so no prompt section, tool schema, tool result, or message text is added, and no model request is made for the stopped step or for any later step while the cap holds. The breach record, the pricing records, and the goal's `budget-exhausted` block reason are durable state for humans and supervising processes; none of them is a surface event, so none reaches a model request.

#### Token effect

Zero added tokens, and the request the stopped step would have sent is never spent.

#### KV Cache effect

Independent: the request surface is neither extended nor rewritten, so an already-reusable prefix stays reusable; the session simply issues no further request while the cap holds.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **Session-scoped only** — the caps measure one session log. A deployment that wants a per-workspace, per-user, or per-day ceiling has no aggregation point here; subagent sessions carry their own logs and their own independent budgets.
- **Cost covers priced routes only** — usage on a `provider/model` absent from `pricing` adds tokens but no cost and records no `usage/priced`, so `maxCostEur` cannot be the sole ceiling for a deployment whose routes are not all priced, and an unpriced session has no cost the log can state.
- **A turn that ends by error or abort leaves its last step unpriced** — pricing happens at the next pre-step or at the normal stop boundary, and neither is reached when a turn fails or is cancelled. The record lands at the session's next pre-step or stop; a session abandoned right after such a turn keeps one unpriced step.
- **One input rate per route** — the table prices billed input with a single number, so a provider that discounts cache reads against cache misses is priced at the uncached rate.
- **No warning before the stop** — the policy has no advisory threshold that tells the model to wrap up before the cap trips; the first model-visible consequence of an exhausted budget is that the turn ends.
- **Raising a cap needs a reload** — configured caps are load-time configuration, so an exhausted session resumes only after the deployment is reconfigured and reloaded; a `budget/caps` record can only tighten, so there is no runtime grant either.
- **No session-cap authority** — any writer of a session's log can record `budget/caps`, and the record is honoured because it can only narrow. Nothing states which orchestrator owns a session's caps, so two writers on one session simply compose by last-wins-then-tighten.

import Loader from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'

import type { Agent, PreStepDecision } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'

import * as budgetPolicy from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
